wc.text: The timing of revenue recognition depends on the nature of each performance obligation. A distinct license is typically satisfied at a point in time, upon delivery of the license and the resulting ability of the customer to use and benefit from it. A combined performance obligation that includes research and development services is typically satisfied over time. For performance obligations satisfied over time, the Company measures progress using an input method, typically based on costs incurred relative to total estimated costs to satisfy the performance obligation. The Company reassesses the measure of progress each reporting period, with any change accounted for as a change in estimate on a cumulative catch-up basis. Significant management judgment is required in determining the level of effort or cost required to satisfy the performance obligations under an arrangement, including the identification of costs that depict progress toward satisfaction. Consideration received, or unconditionally due, in advance of the satisfaction of a performance obligation is recorded as contract liability, presented as deferred revenue, and is recognized as revenue as that performance obligation is satisfied. A contract asset is recorded when the Company satisfies a performance obligation before the right to the related consideration becomes unconditional.

rd.text: Research and development expenses consist of candidate costs, discovery costs, salaries, facilities-related costs, stock-based compensation, and depreciation and amortization. Candidate costs are costs incurred to advance certain drug candidates through preclinical and clinical development. They consist primarily of outsourced costs related to the manufacturing of clinical supplies, toxicity and efficacy studies, and clinical trial expenses. Discovery costs are costs incurred for research activities to identify and evaluate potential new drug candidates before a certain candidate has been selected for development, and consist primarily of laboratory-related expenses. Salaries consist of compensation and related benefits for research and development personnel. Facilities-related costs consist primarily of costs associated with the Company’s research facilities in California and Wisconsin, where its internal research and development activities, primarily discovery operations, are conducted. Stock-based compensation and depreciation and amortization are non-cash expenses and are presented separately in the table below.

ga.text:

Salaries expense increased $30.6 million, or 96%, for the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period of 2025. The increase was driven by higher headcount required to support the Company's commercialization of REDEMPLO, as well as annual salary increases.

Professional, outside services, and other expenses include costs related to commercial activities, legal, consulting, patent filings, business insurance, other external services, as well as travel, communication, and technology expenses. Facilities related expense primarily includes rental costs and other facilities-related costs for the Company’s corporate headquarters in Pasadena, California. These expenses increased $2.5 million, or 44%, for the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period of 2025.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense)
nonop.text: Other income (expense), net consists primarily of interest income, interest expense, losses on the Company’s equity method investment in Bisirna, and the gain on Visirna’s sale of IPR&D assets. Other income (expense), net improved by $30.1 million for the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period of 2025. The improvement was primarily due to interest income earned on the Company's available-for-sale securities and gain on Visirna's sale of IPR&D assets, partially offset by non-cash interest on liability related to the sale of future royalties and loss on equity method investment.

net.text: Net loss attributable to Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was $724.2 million for the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to a net loss attributable to Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. of $1.6 million for the year ended September 30, 2025. Diluted net loss per share was $5.11 for the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to diluted net loss per share of $0.01 for the year ended September 30, 2025. The increase in net loss attributable to Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. for the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period of 2025 was primarily due to expense related to the acquired priority review voucher, lower collaboration and license revenue, higher selling, general and administrative expenses primarily associated with commercialization activities, and higher research and development expenses driven by the expansion of the Company’s pipeline and the progression of programs through clinical trials. These increases were partially offset by lower total other expense, and lower income tax expense.

Cash used in investing activities amounted to $670.5 million, which was primarily attributable to purchases of available-for-sale securities of $1,138.7 million, purchase of the priority review voucher of $215.0 million and capital expenditures of $12.0 million, partially offset by proceeds from maturities of available-for-sale securities of $368.5 million and sales of available-for-sale securities of $326.8 million.

wc.text: The timing of revenue recognition depends on the nature of each performance obligation. A distinct license is typically satisfied at a point in time, upon delivery of the license and the resulting ability of the customer to use and benefit from it. A combined performance obligation that includes research and development services is typically satisfied over time. For performance obligations satisfied over time, the Company measures progress using an input method, typically based on costs incurred relative to total estimated costs to satisfy the performance obligation. The Company reassesses the measure of progress each reporting period, with any change accounted for as a change in estimate on a cumulative catch-up basis. Significant management judgment is required in determining the level of effort or cost required to satisfy the performance obligations under an arrangement, including the identification of costs that depict progress toward satisfaction. Consideration received, or unconditionally due, in advance of the satisfaction of a performance obligation is recorded as contract liability, presented as deferred revenue, and is recognized as revenue as that performance obligation is satisfied. A contract asset is recorded when the Company satisfies a performance obligation before the right to the related consideration becomes unconditional.

The change was primarily driven by a decrease in revenue recognition associated with the Sarepta and Sanofi collaboration and license agreements, and partially offset by an increase in revenue recognition associated with the Novartis and Madrigal collaboration and license agreements, as well as an increase in product revenue from REDEMPLO sales.

Rights to REDEMPLO in Greater China are held by Sanofi under a license from the Company. Majority of our product revenue for fiscal 2026 was generated in the United States.

s.t: As of September 30, 2026, the carrying value of the Company’s investment in Bisirna was $ 7.5 million, which was included in other assets in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.
Other income (expense), net consists primarily of interest income, interest expense, losses on the Company’s equity method investment in Bisirna, and the gain on Visirna’s sale of IPR&D assets.
As of September 30, 2026, the Company had an equity method investment in Bisirna Therapeutics, Inc. (“Bisirna”).

On January 2, 2026, Visirna option holders exercised 14,000,000 stock options, which decreased the Company’s ownership interest in Visirna from 66.25 % to 56.38 % and constituted a reconsideration event.
As a result, the Company’s ownership interest in Visirna decreased from 66.25 % to 56.38 %.
As a result, the Company's ownership interest in Bisirna decreased from approximately 25.3 % to approximately 19.3 %.

The Company concluded that it continues to have the ability to exercise significant influence over Bisirna's operating and financial policies, and therefore continues to account for its investment in Bisirna under the equity method.
